newsitem.title: INDIA: Four killed in police firing, clashes in India.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in police firing, clashes in India.

text.p: Troops imposed a curfew on an area of northeastern India on Thursday after four people were killed and at least 20 injured in police firing and ethnic violence, police said.

Dilip Debbarma, police chief in Tripura state's capital Agartala, said supporters of the Bengali fundamentalist Amra Bangalee party ransacked a government office and attacked police in nearby Khowai area.
They were protesting against the alleged kidnapping of some businessmen by tribal militants this week, he said.
"At least 15 people were injured when police opened fire to disperse the violent mob," he told Reuters in the eastern city of Calcutta by telephone. "Two of the injured later died in hospital."
Debbarma said Amra Bangalee supporters then set several tribal houses in a nearby area on fire. Two people were killed and five injured in the attack, he said.
"The army has been deployed and prohibitory orders have been clamped in the area to prevent any further violence," Debbarma said.
